newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Sears plans 370 mln stg payout.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Sears plans 370 mln stg payout.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc on Tuesday said it planned to hand shareholders about 370 million stg after completion of the sale of its Freemans home shopping business to Littlewoods LWD.CN.
The payout plans would include a restructuring of Sears' capital, chairman Sir Bob Reid said in an interview.
Reid said the company had got clearance from the Inland Revenue for the plan. Earlier the company announced it was
Sears also unveiled plans to try and revive its fortunes by rationalising loss-making British Shoe Corporation and demerging Selfridges department store.
Reid said the demerger would go ahead towards the middle of next year and described recent estimates valuing Selfridges' at around 600 million stg as "conservative."
"We're looking for a lot more than that," he told Reuters, "It's a way above 600 million."
On British Shoe Reid said Sears had brought in David James as executive chairman, with a track record of looking at underperforming assets.
James would look at each of the shoe businesses and see what their value was in the open market, look at the advantages of holding on to them, or selling them, Reid said.
He said it was too early to say what the cost might be to Sears of the rationalisation. "We would deal with the provisions when we've actually gone through the shoe businesses one by one."
Reid also declined to make any predictions on job cuts which might follow the restructuring.
He said there might be management job losses but this was all he could see at this stage. He said Sears wanted to complete the rationalisation by the end of this year.
Reid said there was a range of people interested in BSC, including its real estate. He said U.S. shoe retailers Nine West Group and Payless Shoesource had expressed an interest.
Sears planned to keep all its clothing businesses, which include Wallis, Warehouse, Richards and childrenswear chain Adams, the chairman said.

Reid said chief executive Liam Strong, who is stepping down, would leave the company in the near future. Strong's departure had long been anticipated as he increasingly came under attack for failing to deliver a promised turnaround in Sears' performance after five years in the job.
Reid said he would stay on as chairman. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
